title: Soil texture and erosion on a test slope

stimulus.title: Pilot results: soil washed off three soil trays

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A class wants to know how soil texture affects how much soil is washed away by heavy rain. They fill three identical trays with soil (sandy soil, loam and silt loam), each 5 cm deep, and tilt every tray to the same 15° slope. A watering can with a sprinkler head pours 2 L of water on each tray over 2 minutes, and the class collects the muddy water that runs off the bottom, dries it and weighs the soil. A pilot run with one tray of each soil gave the results in the graph. Identify the independent variable in this investigation.

rubric.point: Soil texture (the type of soil in the tray: sandy soil, loam or silt loam)
accept: the type of soil
the share of sand, silt and clay

parts.sample: The independent variable is soil texture: whether the tray holds sandy soil, loam or silt loam.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Identify the dependent variable in this investigation.

rubric.point: The mass of soil washed off the tray (the dry mass of soil in the collected runoff)
accept: grams of soil eroded
the amount of soil lost from each tray

parts.sample: The dependent variable is the mass, in grams, of soil washed off each tray, measured by drying and weighing the soil in the runoff.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Write a testable hypothesis that matches the pilot results.

rubric.point: A statement with a direction linking texture (the share of silt, or of sand) to the mass of soil washed off; not a question, not "affects"
accept: If the silt content of the soil increases, then the mass of soil washed off will increase
Sandy soil will lose less soil to runoff than silt loam

parts.sample: If the share of silt in the soil increases (and the share of sand decreases), then the mass of soil washed off the tray will increase, because water soaks into silty soil more slowly than into sand, so more of it runs off, and fine, loose silt particles are easily carried by moving water.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Identify one variable the class kept constant, and explain why keeping it constant matters.

rubric.point: A constant from the design: the slope of the tray (15°), the depth of soil (5 cm), the volume of water (2 L), the time of watering (2 minutes) or the size of the trays
accept: the angle of the trays
the amount of water poured

rubric.point: Explains that if it changed it would change the amount of soil washed off too, so the result could not be linked to soil texture alone
accept: so only soil texture differs between trays
so differences come from the soil, not the setup

parts.sample: The slope of every tray was kept at 15°. A steeper tray would make the water run off faster and wash away more soil whatever the texture, so keeping the slope the same means any difference in soil washed off can be linked to soil texture.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: The pilot run used one tray of each soil. Describe one change to the design that would make the results more reliable.

rubric.point: Repeat trials: use several trays of each soil (or repeat the test several times) and average the results
accept: use three or more trays of each soil
repeat each test and take the mean

parts.sample: Use at least three trays of each soil type and average the mass washed off each type, so one unusual tray does not decide the result.

parts.label: f
parts.prompt: The class repeats the test on the loam, but this time they tilt the trays to 30° instead of 15°. Predict how the mass of soil washed off will change, and explain your prediction.

rubric.point: Predicts that the mass of soil washed off will increase
accept: more soil will be eroded
soil loss will rise

rubric.point: Explains that on a steeper slope water runs off faster (less time to soak in), with more force to pick up and carry soil particles
accept: faster runoff carries more soil
less infiltration, so more runoff

parts.sample: The mass of soil washed off will increase. On a 30° slope the water runs downhill faster, so less of it soaks in and the faster-moving water has more force to pick up and carry soil particles off the tray.

parts.label: g
parts.prompt: A farmer's field has the same silt loam as the class's silt loam tray and sits on a slope beside a stream. Describe one environmental effect on the stream of the soil loss shown in the graph, and explain how the soil loss causes it.

rubric.point: An effect on the stream: more sediment (cloudier water), fish eggs or gravel beds buried, less light for aquatic plants, or more nutrients or pesticides carried in
accept: increased turbidity
silt smothers fish spawning areas

rubric.point: Explains the link: runoff from the field carries eroded soil into the stream, where it is suspended or settles on the stream bed
accept: eroded soil is washed into the stream by runoff
the sediment blocks sunlight, so plants photosynthesize less

parts.sample: The stream would carry more sediment. Rain that does not soak into the silt loam runs off the field and carries the fine, eroded soil into the stream. The suspended sediment makes the water cloudy, which blocks sunlight from underwater plants, and when it settles it buries the gravel where fish lay their eggs.
